newsitem.title: INDIA: India's NSDL announces fee structure for services.
newsitem.headline: India's NSDL announces fee structure for services.

text.p: India's National Securities Depository Ltd on Wednesday announced a fee structure for the services it proposes to offer.
India's first depository -- which is being set up to usher in paperless trading on bourses -- is scheduled to begin operations on October 31.
NSDL said depository participants will make a security deposit of 100 million rupees, besides paying an entrance fee of 25,000 rupees.

Participants will pay an annual fee of 100,000 rupees, 250,000 rupees or 500,000 rupees for the value of assets handled ranging upto two billion rupees, between 2.0 and 5.0 billion and above 5.0 billion respectively.
The depository -- which is promoted by the National Stock Exchange, Industrial Development Bank of India and Unit Trust of India -- it would not charge issuers or their registrars.
Transaction related fees prescribed payable by the participants to the depository include:
* A settlement fee of 0.5 rupees per 100 rupees value of net deliveries received by the participant. No fee will be payable to the delivering participant.

* Custody fee of 0.7 rupees per 100 rupees per annum on the average value of securities held in custody by the participant. This fee will be collected quarterly on the basis on average holding during the quarter.
* Settlement fee for the off market transactions will be payable at the rate of 0.1 percent subject to a minimum of 10,000 rupees per transaction.
